1 Python JSON practice json.load, json.dump, lists, dictionaries, and safe file rewrites.

Use generic Python examples first

Use these small examples to get comfortable with the read-edit-write cycle before you bring JSON anywhere near the real app.

This is a practice page. The goal is to understand the storage model clearly enough that the later build feels deliberate.

Key words and definitions

TermMeaning
json.loadReads JSON text into a Python structure.
json.dumpWrites a Python structure back to JSON text.
DictionaryA Python key-value structure often used after loading JSON.
ListAn ordered Python sequence often used for many JSON records.
File rewriteSaving the updated document back to storage.

Python JSON tools you need

CodeWhat it doesWhy it matters here
with open(...)Opens a file safely and closes it when the block ends.The project backend will use this repeatedly.
json.load(file)Turns JSON text into Python data.You cannot loop through the file until it has been loaded.
json.dump(data, file, indent=2)Writes Python data back to JSON text.This is how changes become permanent.
append()Adds one new item to a Python list.Useful when creating a new record in JSON storage.

Generic read-edit-write pattern

import json

with open("records.json", "r") as file:
  data = json.load(file)

data.append({
  "id": 3,
  "label": "Example item"
})

with open("records.json", "w") as file:
  json.dump(data, file, indent=2)
data

After loading, JSON is now a Python structure you can loop through or update.

append

This adds one new object to the list in memory.

indent=2

Indentation makes the saved file readable for humans.

What needs care

  • Duplicate ids if identifier management is weak.
  • Broken files if writes are interrupted or structured poorly.
  • Inconsistent nested data if validation rules are unclear.

Practise this in order

This is still a docs-and-practice page. Use it to get comfortable before the real HL backend begins.

Step 1 Practice JSON file

Load one harmless file first

  • Open a simple JSON file containing a small array of objects.
  • Read it into Python and explain whether the result is now a list, a dictionary, or a combination.
Step 2 Python script

Append and rewrite one record carefully

  • Add one new object to the list in memory.
  • Write the whole structure back and inspect the resulting file.

Ask yourself

  • Why do you usually rewrite the whole JSON document rather than one line in the middle?
  • What would happen if two objects shared the same id?

What should be secure before the modelling comparison

  • The class can describe the read-edit-write cycle for a JSON file.
  • Everyone understands why identifiers and validation still matter in a flexible document structure.
  • The difference between updating JSON and updating SQL rows is clear before modelling comparison begins.
